reference_role: edit target and visual style reference
prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Edit target / style reference: the attached ContextLedger Audit System slide. Create a completely updated, polished full-English 16:9 presentation diagram at high resolution (ideally 3840 x 2160). Preserve its visual identity: pale mint/white background, white rounded panels and cards, subtle mint glow/shadows, emerald/teal line icons and arrows, near-black headings, slate blue-grey secondary text, modern clean sans-serif typography. Preserve ContextLedger top left and small 04 badge top right. It should look like a matching new slide in the same deck. All typography must be crisp and readable, ample whitespace, clean arrow routing. NO Chinese anywhere.
This is an updated software architecture diagram, NOT a screenshot. Replace ALL obsolete text and flows, especially the old redaction/current-business-document-access branch. Only use the implemented content specified below. Do not include redaction, withholding fields, current business evidence/version access checks, blockchain, external anchoring, external immutable storage, or claims of successful breaches.

HEADER exact text:
ContextLedger
Audit System
Trace activity, explain changes, and inspect recorded history
04

Two large horizontal panels: Record above, Inspect below. Header occupies about 16%, Record 39%, Inspect 40%, with remaining margin. Build the content with hierarchy and legibility rather than tiny text.

RECORD PANEL:
Heading "Record"
Subtitle "Four event types · One verified audit ledger"
Across the top, four event cards with simple green line icons. The first two have slightly stronger green emphasis; the last two have softer neutral mint styling.
Card 1 title "Information access"; body "Search · Q&A · Original opens".
Card 2 title "Permission changes"; body lines "Actor → Employee" and "Before → After · Permission epoch".
Card 3 title "Document updates"; body "Job · Old/new version · Outcome".
Card 4 title "Unauthorised attempts"; body "Endpoint · Reason · Blocked result".
Each of the four event types feeds the SAME transaction/ledger flow. Below the four cards, show left-to-right:
"Transactional append" → three small hash-linked event cards "Event 1" → "Event 2" → "Event 3" → "Integrity check".
Each event card can show "previous_hash", a chain-link icon, and "event_hash" (do not invent real-looking exact values). Make the links explicit and unambiguous.
Below or beside the chain a database capsule: "Local checkpoint" / "Count + head hash", linked to the integrity checker.
Integrity check subtext "Hash chain + checkpoint".
Keep this compact, technical but readable. The ledger is local and tamper-evident, not an external blockchain.

INSPECT PANEL:
Heading "Inspect"
Subtitle "Ask across all four types, or filter each section independently"
A single readable left-to-right sequence of six cards, with green connector arrows:
1. "Audit inquiry"
   "AI question or filters"
   "Employee · Actor · Time"
   "Source · Project · Document"
2. "Administrator"
   "Role + current epoch"
   "Verify audit chain"
3. "Exact SQL query"
   "Filters · Counts · Groups"
   "Stable pagination"
4. "Recorded history"
   "Questions · Answers · Evidence"
   "Permission before → after"
   "Versions · Outcomes"
5. "AI interpretation"
   "Up to 20 representative events"
   "Exact totals from all matches"
6. "Traceable answer"
   "[E123] Event details"
   "[Q1] Query statistics"
Use appropriate consistent line icons, no decorative clutter. AI is read-only; SQL statistics are computed by the backend, not guessed by AI.
Below this flow, a thin mint explanatory strip:
"Full recorded history remains auditable after revocation."
A smaller but readable line:
"Role, epoch and chain are checked again before delivery."
Route one neat return arrow around the outside of the cards from the Inspect flow back to Transactional append; label it "Audit inquiries are logged". Avoid crossing cards or text.
If needed for space, use the cards' text exactly but adjust line breaks. Do not add unsupported features. Do not imply that administrators need business source access to audit prior records, or that searches prove personal reading. Keep the diagram elegant and balanced like the reference image.
